title: The Invisible Living World: Beyond Our Naked Eye

learn.hook: A single spoonful of garden soil can hold many millions of tiny living things. You just cannot see them without help!
points: Microorganisms (microbes) are living things too small to see with the naked eye. We need a microscope to see most of them.
The main groups are bacteria, fungi, protozoa, algae and viruses. Many are single-celled; some fungi and algae are many-celled.
Examples: Lactobacillus is a bacterium, yeast and bread mould are fungi, Amoeba and Paramecium are protozoa, and Spirogyra is an alga.
Viruses are even smaller than bacteria. They can multiply only inside the cells of another living thing.
Microbes live almost everywhere: in soil, water, air, inside our bodies, and even in very hot springs and icy places.

example.q: Think it through: Your mother keeps a slice of bread in a warm, damp box for a few days and a fuzzy greyish-green layer appears. Is this a living thing? Which group does it belong to?
steps: The fuzzy layer appeared and grew over days, so it is growing, which living things do.
It needed warmth and moisture, like many microbes.
Fuzzy threads on bread are typical of bread mould, which is a fungus.
example.answer: Yes, it is bread mould, a living fungus. (Mouldy food should not be eaten or sniffed closely.)

learn.reallife: Green slime on a pond or on the walls of a water tank is often algae, and the black spots on old, damp bread are fungi.

games.title: Microbe facts
items: Most microorganisms can be seen only with a microscope.
They are too small for the naked eye.
Viruses can multiply on their own outside any living cell.
Viruses can multiply only inside the cells of a host.
Microbes are found in air, water and soil.

quiz.q: Which of these is a fungus?
quiz.explain: Yeast is a single-celled fungus. Amoeba is a protozoan, Lactobacillus a bacterium and Spirogyra an alga.
steps: Yeast is a single-celled fungus
Amoeba is a protozoan, Lactobacillus a bacterium and Spirogyra an alga
Answer: Yeast
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the groups of microorganisms

quiz.q: Which group of microbes can multiply only inside the cells of another living thing?
quiz.explain: Viruses do not multiply on their own. They use the host's cells to make copies of themselves.
steps: Viruses cannot multiply on their own
They multiply only inside the cells of another living thing
Answer: Viruses
quiz.mistake: Thinks all microbes reproduce in the same way

quiz.q: Why do we need a microscope to see bacteria?
options: Bacteria are far too small for our eyes
quiz.explain: Bacteria are only a few micrometres long, so a microscope must magnify them for us to see them.
steps: Bacteria are only a few micrometres long
Our eyes cannot see things that small, so a microscope must magnify them
Answer: Bacteria are far too small for our eyes
quiz.mistake: Thinks microbes are hidden for reasons other than their size

quiz.q: Amoeba belongs to which group?
quiz.explain: Amoeba is a single-celled protozoan that moves with false feet.
steps: Amoeba is single-celled and moves with false feet
It belongs to the protozoa
Answer: Protozoa
quiz.mistake: Thinks every single-celled organism is a bacterium

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a microorganism?
quiz.explain: An earthworm is easily seen with the naked eye. Paramecium, bread mould and Lactobacillus are all microorganisms.
steps: Microorganisms are too small to see with the naked eye
An earthworm is easily seen, so it is not a microorganism
Answer: Earthworm
quiz.mistake: Thinks any small soil animal is a microbe

quiz.q: Green slimy growth in a pond is most likely made of:
quiz.explain: Algae contain chlorophyll, which makes them green. They grow well in still water with sunlight.
steps: Algae contain chlorophyll, which makes them green
They grow well in still water with sunlight, forming green slime
Answer: Algae
quiz.mistake: Does not link green colour with algae

quiz.q: Which statement about where microbes live is correct?
options: Almost everywhere, including soil, water, air and our bodies
quiz.explain: Microbes are found nearly everywhere, even inside our intestines, where many help us.
steps: Microbes live in soil, water, air and inside our bodies
So they are found almost everywhere, not only in dirty or hot places
Answer: Almost everywhere, including soil, water, air and our bodies
quiz.mistake: Thinks microbes live only in dirty places

quiz.q: Which microbe group includes many-celled forms such as mushrooms and moulds?
quiz.explain: Fungi include single-celled yeast and many-celled moulds and mushrooms.
steps: Fungi include single-celled yeast
and many-celled moulds and mushrooms
Answer: Fungi
quiz.mistake: Thinks all microbe groups are single-celled

teach.ask: Gappu peeks at a puddle: Mama says the water is full of life, but I see nothing! What are these hidden living things?
teach.praise: Wow, tiny microbes like bacteria and algae live in my puddle and I need a microscope to see them. Hello, little friends!
teach.nudge: What are these living things called, and why can't I see them? Can you name some kinds?

learn.hook: In 1665 Robert Hooke looked at a thin slice of cork and saw rows of tiny boxes. He called them 'cells', and biology was never the same again!
points: The cell is the basic unit of life. All living things are made of one cell (unicellular, like Amoeba) or many cells (multicellular, like us).
Robert Hooke named cells in 1665. Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, using his own lenses, was the first to see living microbes.
Most cells have a cell membrane (outer boundary), cytoplasm (jelly-like filling) and a nucleus (control centre).
Plant cells also have a cell wall, chloroplasts (where food is made using sunlight) and usually a large vacuole. Animal cells do not have a cell wall.
A light microscope magnifies using two lenses. Total magnification = eyepiece magnification × objective magnification.

example.q: Think it through: A microscope has a 10× eyepiece and a 40× objective lens. How many times bigger does a cell look?
steps: Each lens magnifies in turn, so we multiply.

learn.reallife: Pathology labs use microscopes to look at blood cells when a doctor orders a blood test.

quiz.q: Who first used the word 'cell' after looking at cork?
quiz.explain: Robert Hooke studied a thin slice of cork in 1665 and called the tiny boxes cells.
steps: Robert Hooke looked at a thin slice of cork in 1665
He called the tiny boxes 'cells'
Leeuwenhoek was the first to see living microbes, not the one who named cells
Answer: Robert Hooke
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Hooke, who named cells, with Leeuwenhoek, who first saw living microbes

quiz.q: In which year did Robert Hooke describe cells in cork?
quiz.explain: Hooke published his observations of cork cells in 1665.
steps: Hooke published his observations of cork cells
The year was 1665
Answer: 1665
quiz.mistake: Guesses the century of the discovery

quiz.q: Which part is found in a plant cell but NOT in an animal cell?
quiz.explain: Plant cells have a cell wall outside the cell membrane. Animal cells have only a cell membrane.
steps: Plant and animal cells both have a nucleus, membrane and cytoplasm
Only plant cells have a cell wall outside the membrane
Answer: Cell wall
quiz.mistake: Thinks the cell membrane and the cell wall are the same thing

quiz.q: Which part of the cell controls its activities?
quiz.explain: The nucleus is the control centre of the cell.
steps: The nucleus is the control centre of the cell
So it controls the cell's activities
Answer: Nucleus
quiz.mistake: Thinks the cytoplasm or cell wall controls the cell

quiz.q: A microscope has a 10× eyepiece and a 10× objective. How many times bigger does the specimen appear?
steps: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective
Answer: 100
quiz.explain: Magnifications of the two lenses are multiplied, not added.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two magnifications instead of multiplying them

quiz.q: Amoeba is called unicellular because:
options: It is made of one cell
It has one nucleus in each of its many cells
quiz.explain: Uni means one. An Amoeba's whole body is just one cell that does all life activities.
steps: Uni means one
Amoeba's whole body is a single cell, so it is unicellular
Answer: It is made of one cell
quiz.mistake: Misreads 'unicellular' as a word about lifestyle instead of cell number

quiz.q: Green chloroplasts are found in the cells of:
quiz.explain: Leaf cells have chloroplasts that capture sunlight to make food. Animal cells do not have them.
steps: Chloroplasts capture sunlight to make food in plant cells
A tulsi leaf is a plant part; cheek, egg and bone cells are animal cells
Answer: A tulsi leaf
quiz.mistake: Thinks animal cells also make food using sunlight

quiz.q: Which correctly lists levels from smaller to larger?
quiz.explain: Similar cells form a tissue, and different tissues together form an organ.
steps: Similar cells together form a tissue
Different tissues together form an organ
So cell → tissue → organ
Answer: Cell, tissue, organ
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order of cells, tissues and organs

teach.ask: Gappu blinks: Everyone says I am made of cells. What is a cell, and what is inside it?
teach.praise: So cells are my tiny building blocks, each with a nucleus as boss and a membrane as its fence. Amazing!
teach.nudge: What is a cell to a living thing, and what parts does it have inside?

learn.hook: The fluffy idli on your plate, the curd in your raita and the medicine that cured your infection all owe something to microbes!
points: Lactobacillus bacteria turn milk into curd. Yeast and bacteria ferment idli and dosa batter, and the gas they make (carbon dioxide) makes batter and bread dough rise.
Rhizobium bacteria live in the root nodules of pulse plants (legumes) like gram and peas and fix nitrogen from the air, making the soil richer.
Decomposer microbes break down dead plants, animals and kitchen waste into compost (manure), returning nutrients to the soil.
Antibiotics such as penicillin are made from microbes. Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin from a mould in 1928. Antibiotics work against bacteria, not viruses.
Harmful microbes (pathogens) cause diseases: typhoid and cholera (bacteria), common cold and flu (viruses), malaria (a protozoan). Some microbes also spoil food.

example.q: Think it through: Why do we keep cooked dal in the refrigerator overnight rather than on the kitchen shelf?
steps: Microbes from the air settle on food and grow on it.
They grow and multiply fastest in warm conditions.
Cold slows their growth, so the dal stays fresh for longer.
example.answer: Low temperature slows the growth of the microbes that spoil food.

learn.reallife: Pickles last for months because salt, oil and spices stop most microbes from growing. Jams use lots of sugar for the same reason.

quiz.q: Which microbe helps convert milk into curd?
quiz.explain: Lactobacillus bacteria multiply in milk and turn it into curd.
steps: Lactobacillus bacteria multiply in milk
They turn milk into curd
Answer: Lactobacillus
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the useful bacteria and their roles

quiz.q: Why does idli batter rise when kept overnight?
options: The rice swells with water only
Microbes ferment it and release carbon dioxide gas
It absorbs air from the room
quiz.explain: Fermenting microbes make carbon dioxide, and its bubbles make the batter rise and soft.
steps: Yeast and bacteria ferment the batter overnight
Fermentation releases carbon dioxide gas, whose bubbles make it rise
Answer: Microbes ferment it and release carbon dioxide gas
quiz.mistake: Thinks the batter rises only by soaking up water

quiz.q: Rhizobium bacteria help plants by:
options: Fixing nitrogen from the air into the soil
quiz.explain: Rhizobium lives in root nodules of legumes and converts nitrogen from the air into a form plants can use.
steps: Rhizobium lives in root nodules of legumes like gram and peas
It fixes nitrogen from the air into a form plants can use, enriching the soil
Answer: Fixing nitrogen from the air into the soil
quiz.mistake: Does not know the role of nitrogen-fixing bacteria

quiz.q: Who discovered penicillin?
quiz.explain: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin from a Penicillium mould in 1928.
steps: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin
He found it from a Penicillium mould in 1928
Answer: Alexander Fleming
quiz.mistake: Confuses Fleming with Jenner, who developed the smallpox vaccine

quiz.q: Antibiotics will NOT cure which of these?
quiz.explain: The common cold is caused by viruses, and antibiotics act on bacteria, not viruses.
steps: Antibiotics act on bacteria, not on viruses
The common cold is caused by viruses, so antibiotics will not cure it
Typhoid and cholera are bacterial
Answer: Common cold
quiz.mistake: Thinks antibiotics kill every kind of germ

quiz.q: Malaria is caused by:
quiz.explain: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium, which is spread by the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
steps: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium
Plasmodium is a protozoan, spread by female Anopheles mosquitoes
Answer: A protozoan
quiz.mistake: Thinks the mosquito itself is the cause, or that malaria is viral

quiz.q: What do decomposer microbes do in a compost pit?
quiz.explain: Decomposers break down plant and food waste into compost that enriches soil. They cannot break down most plastics.
steps: Decomposers break down plant and food waste
They turn kitchen waste into compost (manure); they cannot break down most plastics
Answer: Turn kitchen waste into manure
quiz.mistake: Thinks microbes can break down plastic just like food waste

quiz.q: Why do pickles made with lots of salt last for months?
options: Salt removes water so most microbes cannot grow
quiz.explain: Salt draws water out of food and microbes, so they cannot grow and spoil the pickle.
steps: Salt draws water out of food and microbes
Without water most microbes cannot grow, so the pickle does not spoil
Answer: Salt removes water so most microbes cannot grow
quiz.mistake: Does not link salt with stopping microbial growth

teach.ask: Gappu frowns: Microbes are bad, right? Should I be scared of all of them?
teach.praise: Ooh! Some microbes make curd and medicines, and only some cause disease. I will wash my wings but not fear every microbe!
teach.nudge: Are ALL microbes bad? Can you tell me some useful jobs they do, and which ones are harmful?

revise.summary: Useful microbes make curd (Lactobacillus), ferment batter (yeast), fix nitrogen (Rhizobium), make compost and give antibiotics like penicillin (Fleming, 1928). Harmful microbes cause diseases such as typhoid, cholera (bacteria), cold, flu (viruses) and malaria (protozoan), and spoil food.

Diseases and the type of microbe that causes each
Antibiotics work on bacteria, not viruses
Ways to slow food spoilage: cold, salt
remember: Lactobacillus → curd; yeast → batter and dough rise (carbon dioxide); Rhizobium → nitrogen fixation in legume root nodules
Penicillin discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928 from a mould
Typhoid, cholera: bacteria; cold, flu: viruses; malaria: protozoan Plasmodium (female Anopheles mosquito)
traps: Antibiotics do not cure viral illnesses like the common cold
Malaria is caused by a protozoan, not a virus or bacterium
Decomposers cannot break down most plastics
